simple.meaning: פִּדְיוֹם (pidyôwm) is a Hebrew word meaning “a ransom.” BibleIQ connects the English word back to this source word so its use can be compared across Scripture.
simple.biblicalBackground: פִּדְיוֹם (H6306) appears 3 times in the Hebrew Bible, beginning at Exodus 21:30, with occurrences in Exodus, Numbers, Psalms.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to פִּדְיוֹם (H6306) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: English translations can use the same English word for different Hebrew words. BibleIQ anchors the study in פִּדְיוֹם (H6306) before moving outward to related references.
simple.summary: פִּדְיוֹם (pidyôwm) / H6306 is traced through Exodus 21:30, Numbers 3:49, Psalms 49:9 using source-language evidence and occurrence comparison.

definitions.full: H6306. pidyowm מִּדְיוֺם noun masculine ransom ; — Num 3:49 , read probably מְּדוּיִם (so ⅏ ); מִּדְיֹם 3:51 Kt (Qr מְּדוּיִם ); — see פדה Qal Passive participle , and מִּדוּיִם above מִּדְיוֺן noun masculine id.; — ׳מּ נֶפֶשׁ Exod 21:30 (E), Psa 49:9 .
definitions.rootNote: or פִּדְיֹם ; also פִּדְיוֹן ; or פִּדְיֹן ; from 6299 ;

occurrences.englishText: If a ransom is imposed on him, then he shall give for the redemption of his life whatever is imposed.
Moses took the redemption money from those who exceeded the number of those who were redeemed by the Levites;
that he should live on forever,
